key_insight: Hyperspectral imaging can separate donor and acceptor signals in roll-to-roll coated organic photovoltaic active layers, enabling real-time spatial quality monitoring during manufacturing.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical inline metrology approach for scalable slot-die coating, supporting process control and defect detection in organic solar cell production.
method: Inline hyperspectral camera on roll-to-roll slot-die coated P3HT/OIDTBR films
Multivariate curve resolution to resolve donor and acceptor spatial distributions
Spectral fitting of P3HT absorbance to map exciton bandwidth and aggregation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reliable spatial separation of P3HT and OIDTBR contributions and successful exciton-bandwidth mapping from hyperspectral absorbance spectra.
watch_item: Inline hyperspectral models may require careful calibration and spectral unmixing robustness to handle coating variability, noise, and changing process conditions.
paper_title: Hyperspectral imaging for inline quality monitoring of roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers
